official_questions.stem: Which one of the following was not a form of industrial capital and colonial exploitation during British rule in India ?

statements.t: Railway construction financed by the British government was not a form of industrial-capital colonial exploitation.
statements.d: Construction of railways was financed by the British government
statements.fact: Railways (built by British companies with guaranteed returns) served market penetration – a form of it.

statements.t: Large British investment in the jute industry was not a form of industrial-capital colonial exploitation.
statements.d: British capitalists invested large amount of money in jute industry
statements.fact: British capital in jute (finance-capital stage) – counted as a form here.

official_questions.rule: Bipan Chandra's stages: mercantile (1757-1813), industrial capital/free trade (1813-1858), finance capital (after 1858).
official_questions.key_note: Debatable: high British duties on Indian textiles persisted into the 19th c.; and railways were financed by private British companies with guaranteed interest from Indian revenues. Key kept.
